purpose: Retain an explicit authority-confirmed occurrence report for evaluated-method admission, not an immutable county evidence run.

findings.claim: CDFA confirmed two Anastrepha suspensa trapped in Long Beach, Los Angeles County between January 20 and February 9, 2026.
The document explicitly dates the first California detections to San Diego County in 1983.
The same document includes general US distribution restricted to peninsular or central/southern Florida while confirming the California detections.
findings.meaning: An actual counterexample to treating general restricted-distribution prose as universal current or historical absence outside its named region.

limitations: The full original PDF is retained. Source wording was read through the PDF text extraction; one browser screenshot request for PDF page 3 failed with Cache miss. No visual signature date is asserted.
March 2026 is printed on the work plan. The day encoded in the filename is not assigned as the declaration date.
Program validity through October 15, 2026 is administrative authorization, not biological persistence or proved eradication.

Specific confirmed trapped organisms can support historical occurrence without obtaining every raw trap record. Independent semantic review and a registered tested adapter are required before integration.
Host lists, treatment boundaries, eradication aspirations and sterile release schedules are not wild occurrence evidence.
No source-silence negatives, establishment determination or research completion was created.
nextAction: Evaluate and register a reusable retained authority-confirmed occurrence-report adapter with independent review, exact catalog/county mapping and original date precision. Pilot these two exact pairs before expanding to the CDFA emergency-program report collection.
